news.title: S&P 500 nears record as yields and oil retreat; rally stays tech-led
news.text: The S&P 500 hit a fresh intraday all-time high Tuesday (6 Oct) and the Nasdaq Composite extended Monday's record close, with the Dow up roughly 190 points (~0.4%). Gains were led by megacap tech names as Treasury yields and crude oil both eased back from their recent multi-year highs, giving the market room to focus on strong AI-driven earnings growth expected this quarter.

footnotes: QQQ (NDX proxy) omitted again this run: one WebSearch result flatly stated 'QQQ closed at $364.70 on Oct 6' (a TradingView notes page) which is wildly inconsistent with FMP's SPX/Nasdaq-adjacent levels and with the brief's own recent QQQ references near $750 - clearly stale or wrong, so left out rather than published with an unreconciled number.

Index futures (ES/NQ/YM/RTY) omitted this run: WebSearch results were a mix of contradictory premarket snapshots (e.g. one source citing Dow futures -0.03% at 6:44pm EDT 'on October 6' - which is after the US close, not before it) and generic multi-year-old archive pages. The cash market opened at 13:30 UTC and this fetch ran at ~13:40-13:51 UTC, 10-20 minutes after the open, so a reconciled premarket futures read wasn't available or current enough to publish; the live cash indices above are the reliable read on the session.

Overnight/sector news was unusually hard to pin to today this run: a 'semiconductor sector selloff' story (Samsung/SK Hynix/Western Digital down sharply) contradicts today's live tape (SKHY -2.1%, ALAB +8.2%, GLW +2.7%, GNRC +3.6%, ARM +1.0% per FMP) and was dropped as stale/mismatched; an Intel/Terafab 'surge' story and a China-chip-export-controls story both came back with no reliable current date (mixed in with April 2026 and undated archive pages) and were dropped for the same reason.
